selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What kind of person is the second brother at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: He is wise, fortunate, and good in character.

questions.question: How did he usually imagine things around him?
questions.answer: He imagined them in a good and hopeful way.

questions.question: What mixed condition did he find in the garden?
questions.answer: The garden had both pleasant things and spoiled, dirty things.

questions.question: Why was he still able to stay steadier than his brother?
questions.answer: He believed the lion was not acting on its own but under authority.

questions.question: What signs of danger surrounded him in the well?
questions.answer: There was a lion above, a dragon below, and two creatures cutting the roots.

questions.question: How is the second traveler described in this passage?
questions.answer: He is shown as lucky, smart, and well-behaved.

questions.question: What place did he come to on his journey?
questions.answer: He came to a garden with both beautiful things and dirty, rotten things.

questions.question: What two opposite kinds of things were in the garden?
questions.answer: There were lovely, useful things and also rotten, filthy things.

questions.question: How did that choice help his journey?
questions.answer: It gave him rest and strength to continue.

questions.question: What was his condition inside the well?
questions.answer: He was hanging in the middle, holding onto a tree.

questions.question: What did he begin to believe that hidden ruler was doing?
questions.answer: He believed the ruler was watching him, testing him, and leading him for a reason.

questions.question: What was strange about the fig tree he saw?
questions.answer: One tree seemed to carry the fruits of many thousands of trees.

questions.question: How did the dragon and lion change?
questions.answer: They became like servants, and the lion even became a gentle riding animal.

questions.question: What is one main difference between the two brothers in this passage?
questions.answer: One thinks in a good and wise way, while the other thinks in a bad and foolish way.

questions.question: What mix of things did he find in the garden?
questions.answer: He found pretty and useful things along with rotten and dirty things.

questions.question: What happened because he paid attention to the good things in the garden?
questions.answer: He benefited from them, rested well, and continued peacefully.

questions.question: What good results came from following that rule?
questions.answer: He benefited, rested, and moved on in a better state.

questions.question: What action did he take even though he found some comfort?
questions.answer: He still ran away and jumped into a well.

questions.question: What did he think about the connection between all these strange things?
questions.answer: He thought they were all linked and directed by one hidden ruler.

questions.question: What did he ask for before making his prayer?
questions.answer: He asked to be shown the key to the mystery.

questions.question: What personal qualities make the second brother different from the first?
questions.answer: He has intelligence, good manners, and a hopeful outlook.

questions.question: What did he discover in the garden?
questions.answer: He discovered both pleasant things and dirty, decaying things.

questions.question: What does this show about his way of thinking?
questions.answer: It shows he tried to see the better side of things.

questions.question: What thought gave him comfort when he saw the lion?
questions.answer: He thought the desert must have a ruler and the lion might be under that ruler’s command.
